factual_claims.claim: AI programs currently lack human-like intentions, which complicates the application of legal standards that rely on mens rea or intention.
The doctrine of respondeat superior in tort law holds principals liable for the actions of their agents.
OpenAI has been sued for defamation due to ChatGPT hallucinating false crimes about a plaintiff.
The Financial Artificial Intelligence Risk Reduction Act proposes strict liability for security law violations unless reasonable steps were taken to prevent harm.
Contract law has long contemplated that contracts can be created by electronic agents.
The Supreme Court in Counterman v. Colorado held that criminal prosecution for online threats requires showing the defendant subjectively understood the fear they were causing.
